/-!
# Erdős Problem 986

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/986](https://www.erdosproblems.com/986)
- [ChGr98] Chung, F. and Graham, R., *Erdős on Graphs: His Legacy of Unsolved Problems*.
  A K Peters, Ltd. (1998).
- [Br26] Bradač, D., Off-diagonal Ramsey numbers. arXiv:2605.28793 (2026).
- [Sp77] Spencer, J., Asymptotic lower bounds for Ramsey functions. Discrete Math. (1977), 69-76.
- [MaVe23] Mattheus, S. and Verstraëte, J., The asymptotics of $r(4,t)$. Ann. of Math. (2024),
  941-965.
-/

open Filter

namespace Erdos986

/--
For any fixed $s\geq 3$,
$$R(s,k) \gg \frac{k^{s-1}}{(\log k)^c}$$
for some constant $c=c(s)>0$.

According to Chung and Graham [ChGr98] this was first conjectured by Erdős in 1947.

Proved by Bradač [Br26], with $c=2s-4$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_986 :
    ∀ (s : ℕ) (hs : 3 ≤ s),
      ∃ (c C : ℝ), 0 < c ∧ 0 < C ∧
        ∀ᶠ (k : ℕ) in atTop,
          (SimpleGraph.classicalRamsey s k : ℝ) ≥
            C * (k : ℝ) ^ (s - 1) / (Real.log k) ^ c := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Add variants of the problem.

end Erdos986

findings.description: The module bibliography gives pages 941–965 for [MaVe23], Mattheus–Verstraëte, “The asymptotics of r(4,t)” (lines 28–29). The published article occupies pages 919–941. This does not affect the mathematical statement.
findings.source_evidence: The publisher's article page states: “Pages 919-941 from Volume 199 (2024), Issue 2.” https://annals.math.princeton.edu/2024/199-2/p08
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `941-965` with `919-941` in [MaVe23]; optionally include volume 199, issue 2.

reformulations.difference: Lean allows a positive multiplicative constant C, matching the main source's Vinogradov notation. Bradač's introduction quotes the older conjecture with coefficient 1 instead. These formulations are equivalent because the logarithmic exponent c is existential.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Given an eventual bound R(s,k) ≥ C k^(s−1)/(log k)^c with c,C>0, replace c by c+1. Eventually k>1 and log k>1/C, so k^(s−1)/(log k)^(c+1) < C k^(s−1)/(log k)^c ≤ R(s,k). Conversely, a coefficient-one bound gives the Lean bound with C=1. Both the non-strict and strict coefficient-one equivalences were proved in /workspace/review/constant_absorption.lean without using erdos_986.

review.notes: No mathematical misformalization was found in the sole theorem. The solved tag agrees with Erdős Problems and Bradač v3, Theorem 1.1, which supplies c=2s−4. Scratch Lean checks established the ordinary clique/independent-set interpretation, nonemptiness of the Ramsey defining set (excluding the sInf-empty default), the boundary values R(s,0)=0 and R(s,1)=1 for s≥1, eventual positivity of the logarithmic denominator, and equivalence with the usual asymptotic bound. Chung–Graham (2.14) prints log^c k with k fixed—an evident source typo; Erdős Problems and Bradač explicitly use the growing variable. The original [Sp77] full text was blocked by the publisher; it is only a background citation here, and no declaration remained unsettled. The reviewed file was confirmed byte-for-byte identical to the committed version.
